title: Aristotle's passage on the ancestors' belief in divinity

tellings.quote: And and then and then he says, "This shows that our ancestors, our most ancient ancestors were not wrong when they posited that there was a divinity surrounding nature

plain: Aristotle wrote a passage saying that the earliest humans were right to believe in a divine presence in nature. A guest named James Madden paraphrases it for Michels in a conversation about Plato and consciousness: Aristotle "says, 'This shows that our ancestors, our most ancient ancestors were not wrong when they posited that there was a divinity surrounding nature.'" Madden does not say which of Aristotle's works the passage comes from. He uses it to suggest that old beliefs about a divine order may hold real insight.
